entities.summary: Edmund Stafford, 5th Earl of Stafford and 1st Baron Audley, KG, KB, was the son of Hugh de Stafford, 2nd Earl of Stafford, and his wife Philippa de Beauchamp, born into the powerful Stafford family in the 14th century. This noble lineage made him a key player in the politics of medieval England, with his family's lands stretching across the country from Yorkshire to Worcestershire. His early life was marked by the tumultuous reign of King Henry IV, who appointed Edmund as 5th Earl of Stafford in 1398. This appointment brought significant power and influence, as well as the responsibility to support the king's policies. Edmund's leadership during this period was crucial in maintaining the stability of the kingdom, particularly during the Wars of the Roses, which ravaged England from 1455 to 1485. His family's loyalty to the Lancastrian cause ultimately led to their downfall, and Edmund was killed in 1403 during the battle of Shrewsbury. This tragic event marked the end of the Stafford family's reign and had far-reaching consequences for the country. Edmund's legacy lives on through his descendants, who continued to play important roles in English history, including his great-grandson, Henry Stafford, 2nd Duke of Buckingham, who led the Lancastrian faction during the Wars of the Roses. Despite the challenges he faced, Edmund Stafford remained a significant figure in medieval England, embodying the complexities and power struggles of the time. His story serves as a testament to the enduring legacy of the Stafford family, whose influence can still be felt in the modern-day aristocracy and politics.

historicalSignificance.significanceNarrative: Edmund Stafford played a significant role in medieval English politics, particularly during the Wars of the Roses, but ultimately suffered the downfall of the Lancastrian cause. His legacy lives on through his descendants, who continued to shape English history.
